context.title: Josiah's Great Reform
context.summary: Josiah reads the law to the people, renews the covenant, and destroys idolatry across Judah and at Bethel. He keeps a historic Passover but dies facing Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo.
context.background: Josiah died in 609 BC confronting Pharaoh Necho, who was marching north to the Euphrates. Outside records show Egypt was going to support Assyria; the Hebrew word the KJV renders 'against' (v. 29) can also mean 'to.'

customs.note: A site in the Valley of Hinnom where children were sacrificed. The valley's name later became 'Gehenna.'
Renaming a vassal king, as Necho did with Eliakim, showed who was master.

watchFor: Josiah is praised in words echoing Deuteronomy 6:5 — heart, soul and might (v. 25).
Even so, God's anger over Manasseh's sins is not turned away (vv. 26–27).
The prophecy of 1 Kings 13:2 is fulfilled at Bethel, centuries later (vv. 15–18).

w: he had provoked to anger him

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Son of Nun.

people.name: Molech
people.summary: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire.

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:7, 9; 15:29).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Chemosh
people.summary: The destroyer, subduer, or fish-god, the god of the Moabites (Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:7, 13, 46). The worship of this god, “the abomination of Moab,” was introduced at Jerusalem by Solomon (1 Kings 11:7), but was abolished by Josiah (2 Kings 23:13).

people.name: Ashtoreth
people.summary: The moon goddess of the Phoenicians, representing the passive principle in nature, their principal female deity; frequently associated with the name of Baal, the sun-god, their chief male deity (Judg. 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4; 12:10).

people.name: Jeroboam
people.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Jehoahaz
people.summary: A son of king Josiah (1 Chr. 3:15; Jer. 22:11), who was elected to succeed his father on the throne, although he was two years younger than his brother Eliakim.

people.name: Hamutal
people.summary: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: The father of Hamutal (2 Kings 23:31), the wife of Josiah.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.summary: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599).

people.name: Pedaiah
people.summary: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

people.name: Zebudah
people.summary: Given, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Kidron
places.summary: Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives.

places.name: Judah (Southern)
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1257 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Geba
places.summary: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29; Josh. 18:24, 28).

places.name: Judah
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-0611 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: valley of the son of Hinnom
Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:21), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh (Judg. 1:27), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon (1 Kings 4:12; 9:15).

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:29-32; 12:15). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified.

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: Fortress, the capital of one of the kingdoms of Upper Syria of the same name, on the Orontes, in the valley of Lebanon, at the northern boundary of Palestine (Num. 13:21; 34:8), at the foot of Hermon (Josh. 13:5) towards Damascus (Zech. 9:2; Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Riblah
places.summary: Fruitful, an ancient town on the northern frontier of Palestine, 35 miles north-east of Baalbec, and 10 or 12 south of Lake Homs, on the eastern bank of the Orontes, in a wide and fertile plain.

places.name: Rumah
places.summary: Elevation, probably the same as Arumah (Judg. 9:41; 2 Kings 23:36), near Shechem.

events.title: Reign of Josiah
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 22:1–23:30. People: Josiah. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 31 years.

events.title: Death of Josiah
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 23:29. People: Josiah, Pharaoh-nechoh. Place: Megiddo.

events.title: Reign of Johoahaz (Shallum)
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 23:31–35. People: Jehoahaz. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 3 months.

events.title: Reign of Jehoiakim
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 23:36–24:7. People: Jehoiakim. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 11 years.
